reasons: Claimed status is compliant, and no redline or comment was proposed — consistent with the playbook's treatment of compliant findings (retained as internal evidence, not raised as a negotiation issue).

The cited text supports compliance on the rule's material terms: §5.2(a)(ii) imposes an uncapped obligation on MSL to assist in transferring responsibilities and Products to IBM or its designee (better for us than a 6-month cap), §5.2(a)(iii) requires return of all IBM documentation and confidential media within a defined post-termination window, §13.2(c) permits immediate return on demand, and Attachment 6 §3(a) adds a return-plus-written-certification mechanic.

The rule is a 'missing/insert' rule; since a usable transition-assistance and data-return clause plainly exists, classifying as compliant rather than missing is correct, and inserting the model paragraph would be over-flagging.

The failed deterministic check ('data return/transition present') is a phrasing-variant false negative — the quoted paragraphs expressly cover transfer assistance, return of media and certification in non-SaaS 'documentation/media' language rather than 'Customer Data export' wording.

Shortfalls versus the model language (no machine-readable-format specification, certification limited to Attachment 6 media, redacted return period) are correctly noted in the rationale as sub-elements rather than escalated to a deviation, with a stated trigger to revisit if the redacted figure materially exceeds 30 days.
